Summary: Jesus' word to individuals — the man healed at Bethesda and the woman taken in adultery: go, and sin no more. Drafted on its merits with scope stated: spoken to individuals in the moment, and read by many as the general call that pardon carries a changed life.
Application: In both cases pardon or healing is joined to a command, not left bare: grace does not leave the life as it found it. Whether these two personal words form a standing law row or remain narrative pardons is debated, and this row does not settle it.
Purpose: TRADITIONAL reading: to join forgiveness to amendment of life, so that pardon is not taken as licence.
Function: Pardon joined to a command — grace that does not leave the life as it found it. This is a New Testament command, not Mosaic law, so the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it; whether these two personal words form a standing law or remain narrative pardons is debated, and this entry does not settle it. Its goal, on the TRADITIONAL reading, was to join forgiveness to amendment of life. The evil it addressed was pardon taken as licence. It restrained that evil with the word itself: go, and sin no more.
